title: Around town: autos, cabs & the metro
goal: Haggle with an auto driver, tell a driver where to turn and stop, book a cab, find a place by its landmarks, ask how long a trip takes and get around on the metro.
intro:
Getting around a north Indian city is half the adventure: autos that may or may not use the meter, cab apps that ask for an OTP, e-rickshaws for the last stretch, and a metro that is fast, clean and packed. This unit gives you the Hindi for all of it: **भैया, साकेत चलोगे?** 'will you go to Saket?', **मीटर से चलो** 'go by the meter', **अगले सिग्नल से राइट ले लेना** 'take a right at the next light', **यहीं रोक दो** 'stop right here'.

The grammar is two very useful tools: **compound verbs** (रोक **दो**, छोड़ **दो**, बैठ **जाओ**), which make instructions sound natural, and **लगना** for 'it takes' (**कितना टाइम लगेगा?** 'how long will it take?').

grammar.title: Compound verbs: रोक दो, छोड़ दो, बैठ जाओ
grammar.body:
Hindi often follows a verb stem with a second, 'helper' verb. The **stem** carries the meaning; the **helper** loses its own meaning and adds a shade: the action is completed, directed, or simply sounds natural.

**देना** 'give' — the action goes outward or is done for someone else: **रोक दो** 'stop (here)', **छोड़ दो** 'drop (me) off', **बता दो** 'tell (me)'.
**लेना** 'take' — the action is for yourself or comes back to you: **ले लो** 'take it', **राइट ले लेना** 'take a right', **टिकट ले लिया** 'I got the ticket'.
**जाना** 'go' — a change is completed: **बैठ जाओ** 'get in, sit down', **उतर जाना** 'get off', **पहुँच गए** 'we've arrived', **रुक जाओ** 'stop!'

In instructions to a driver, the compound form is what people actually say, and with -इए it is polite: **यहीं रोक दीजिए**. A bare **रोको!** sounds sharp, like an emergency.

**Negatives** normally drop the helper: **मत रोको** 'don't stop' (not मत रोक दो).

The trap: **रोकना** is transitive ('stop something': गाड़ी रोक दो), **रुकना** is intransitive ('stop, wait': रुक जाओ). To a driver, say **रोक दो**.

grammar.title: It takes (time, money): लगना
grammar.body:
To say how long something takes, Hindi uses **लगना**, and the **time is the subject**: the verb agrees with it.

**कितना टाइम लगेगा?** 'how long will it take?'
**आधा घंटा लगेगा** (one thing, masculine) · **दस मिनट लगेंगे** (plural) · **दो घंटे लगते हैं** 'it usually takes two hours'.

**For whom**: the person takes **को** (**मुझे**, **उसे**), like मुझे भूख लगी.
**Doing what**: verb + **-ने में**: **पहुँचने में** 'to get there', **तैयार होने में** 'to get ready'.
मुझे ऑफ़िस पहुँचने में एक घंटा लगता है 'it takes me an hour to get to the office'.

**Money** works the same way: **कितने पैसे लगेंगे?** 'how much will it cost?' — **दो सौ रुपये लगेंगे**.
**From A to B**: **A से B तक**. **Distance**: **कितनी दूर है?** — **पाँच किलोमीटर है** / **ज़्यादा दूर नहीं है**.

The trap: don't translate 'I take an hour' word for word. The time is the subject and the person is **मुझे**: मुझे एक घंटा लगता है.

culture: Call any driver **भैया** 'brother'; he'll call you **सर** or **मैडम**, or **भैया / दीदी** back. Auto meters in many cities are 'broken' by habit, so agree the fare **before** you get in; a ride app open on your phone is the best bargaining tool. Ride apps (Uber, Ola, Rapido for bike taxis) are everywhere: the driver will phone to ask **कहाँ हो?** and **लोकेशन पर आ जाओ**, and won't start until you tell him the **OTP**. Directions are given by **landmarks**, not street names: **मंदिर के पास**, **पेट्रोल पंप के बाद**, **बड़े पीपल के पेड़ से लेफ़्ट**, and in cities **लेफ़्ट / राइट** are more common than दाएँ / बाएँ. On the Delhi Metro the first coach is reserved for women, there's a security check at every entrance, and people will gently push to get on: a polite **ज़रा साइड दीजिए** 'please make way' helps. Most fares today are paid by **UPI**: drivers and even rickshaw-wallahs have a QR code stuck to the vehicle.

tip.title: Agree the fare first
tip.body:
- Call the driver **भैया**. Ask before getting in: **X चलोगे?** 'will you go to X?', then **कितना लोगे?**
- Push back: **बहुत ज़्यादा है**, and offer a price: **सौ रुपये में चलो** (में = 'for').
- Or insist: **मीटर से चलो**.
- Carry small notes: drivers rarely have **छुट्टे**.

tip.title: रोक दो, ले लो, बैठ जाओ
tip.body:
- Add a helper to the stem: **रोक दो** 'stop (here)', **छोड़ दो** 'drop me', **ले लो** 'take', **बैठ जाओ** 'get in'.
- **देना** = outward / for someone, **लेना** = for yourself, **जाना** = a completed change.
- To a driver this is natural and polite: **यहीं रोक दीजिए**. A bare **रोको!** sounds sharp.
- Negative: drop the helper: **मत रोको**.

tip.title: Directions the Indian way
tip.body:
- Places are found by **landmarks**, not street numbers: मंदिर के पास, कोने वाली दुकान.
- **लेफ़्ट / राइट** are more common than दाएँ / बाएँ in cities.
- **इधर** 'this way', **उधर** 'that way', **किधर?** 'which way?' (casual कहाँ).
- **चलाना** = to drive; **चलना** = to go. Don't mix them up.

tip.title: Ride apps in Hindi
tip.body:
- English word + करना: कैब **बुक करना**, बुकिंग **कैंसल करना**.
- The driver will ring: **कहाँ हो?** **लोकेशन पर आ जाओ.**
- Before starting he says **ओटीपी बताइए**: read him the code.
- **खाली** = free, available: कोई कैब **खाली** नहीं है.

tip.title: कितना टाइम लगेगा? — it takes
tip.body:
- Time is the **subject** of **लगना**: आधा घंटा **लगेगा**, दस मिनट **लगेंगे**.
- Usually: **लगता है / लगते हैं**.
- For whom: **मुझे**; doing what: verb + **-ने में**: मुझे तैयार होने **में** दस मिनट लगेंगे.
- Money too: **कितने पैसे लगेंगे?**

sentences.native: घर से ऑफ़िस तक कितना टाइम लगता है?
sentences.roman: ghar se ofis tak kitnā ṭāim lagtā hai?
sentences.en: How long does it take from home to the office?

sentences.native: बस से सिर्फ़ पंद्रह मिनट लगेंगे।
sentences.roman: bas se sirf pandrah minaṭ lageṃge.
sentences.en: By bus it'll only take fifteen minutes.

sentences.native: आज जाम में एक घंटा लग गया।
sentences.roman: āj jām meṃ ek ghaṇṭā lag gayā.
sentences.en: Today I lost an hour in a traffic jam.

sentences.native: मुझे तैयार होने में दस मिनट लगेंगे।
sentences.roman: mujhe taiyār hone meṃ das minaṭ lageṃge.
sentences.en: I'll need ten minutes to get ready.

sentences.native: यहाँ से स्टेशन कितनी दूर है?
sentences.roman: yahāṃ se sṭeshan kitnī dūr hai?
sentences.en: How far is the station from here?

sentences.native: सिर्फ़ दो किलोमीटर है, पैदल चलते हैं।
sentences.roman: sirf do kilomīṭar hai, paidal chalte haiṃ.
sentences.en: It's only two kilometres, let's walk.

sentences.native: हवाई अड्डे तक कितने पैसे लगेंगे?
sentences.roman: havāī aḍḍe tak kitne paise lageṃge?
sentences.en: How much will it cost to the airport?

sentences.native: उसे घर पहुँचने में हमेशा देर लगती है।
sentences.roman: use ghar pahuṃchne meṃ hameshā der lagtī hai.
sentences.en: She always takes ages to get home.

sentences.native: कितना टाइम लगेगा? — बस दस मिनट।
sentences.roman: kitnā ṭāim lagegā? — bas das minaṭ.
sentences.en: How long will it take? — Just ten minutes.

lessons.title: On the metro

tip.title: Metro Hindi
tip.body:
- **मेट्रो** is feminine: मेट्रो **आ गई**.
- Lines go by colour (ब्लू लाइन, येलो लाइन); changing is **लाइन बदलना**.
- A **टोकन** for one trip, a **कार्ड** if you ride often.
- 'Which line?' — **कौन-सी लाइन?** (कौन-सी, because लाइन is feminine).

new: राजीव चौक के लिए कौन-सी लाइन?

sentences.native: मेट्रो आ गई, जल्दी चलो!
sentences.roman: meṭro ā gaī, jaldī chalo!
sentences.en: The metro's here, quick!

sentences.native: राजीव चौक पर लाइन बदलनी पड़ेगी।
sentences.roman: Rājīv Chauk par lāin badalnī paṛegī.
sentences.en: You'll have to change lines at Rajiv Chowk.

sentences.native: एक टोकन ले लो, कार्ड में पैसे नहीं हैं।
sentences.roman: ek ṭokan le lo, kārḍ meṃ paise nahīṃ haiṃ.
sentences.en: Get a token, there's no money on the card.

sentences.native: गेट नंबर तीन से बाहर निकलना।
sentences.roman: geṭ nambar tīn se bāhar nikalnā.
sentences.en: Go out through gate number three.

sentences.native: अगला स्टेशन कौन-सा है? मुझे हौज़ ख़ास पर उतरना है।
sentences.roman: aglā sṭeshan kaun-sā hai? mujhe Hauz Xās par utarnā hai.
sentences.en: What's the next station? I need to get off at Hauz Khas.

sentences.native: मेरा स्टॉप आ गया, मैं उतर रहा हूँ।
sentences.roman: merā sṭop ā gayā, maiṃ utar rahā hūṃ.
sentences.en: This is my stop, I'm getting off.

sentences.native: मेट्रो में बहुत भीड़ है, अगली वाली लेते हैं।
sentences.roman: meṭro meṃ bahut bhīṛ hai, aglī vālī lete haiṃ.
sentences.en: The metro's packed, let's take the next one.

sentences.native: नोएडा के लिए कौन-सी लाइन लूँ?
sentences.roman: Noeḍā ke liye kaun-sī lāin lūṃ?
sentences.en: Which line do I take for Noida?
